_review: DRAFT for the user's review (story: Claude drafts, the user reviews). Every line of text here is a proposal. Rewritten 2026-10-09: quests built on gameplay (fights in waves, an escort, a practice pillar, Echo-stone gestures, a carried flame, Run medals), with consequences in the Warden fight.
title: The Snow That Would Not Fall

npcs.name: Aud
npcs.about: The last keeper of the monastery. Swept the floor around the Shaper's body for nine winters.

npcs.name: Old Maren
npcs.about: Leads the pilgrims. Remembers when snow still fell.

npcs.name: Tobin
npcs.about: A pilgrim child who wanders off following sounds and tracks.

npcs.name: Isolde
npcs.about: Keeps the camp's lantern. Plays the lyre at night.

npcs.name: Varo
npcs.about: A staff-bearer who went out to watch the Warden and did not come back.

npcs.name: Osk
npcs.about: The sled-trader. Drags goods across the ice between the pilgrim fires, and trades for marks and what the cold gives.

aud.wake.speaker: aud
lines: You woke inside the Shaper's robe. I am Aud, keeper of this monastery.
For nine winters I swept around his body. I thought the cloth would rot before it moved.
The three stones in this hall remember a Shaper's hands. Wake one by using its gesture on it: Crystallize, Sweep or Ribbon.
Be careful. Something is listening at the bottom of the steps.

aud.cloister.speaker: aud
lines: The Shaped are climbing the steps now. They never did while he lay here.
Rest at the shrine by the east wall. If you fall, you will wake there.
Then take the Run down to the pilgrims' fire. The Shapers went that way. Lean forward and the slope will carry you.

aud.go.speaker: aud
lines: Rest at the shrine, then take the Run. Lean forward and the slope will carry you.

aud.again.speaker: aud
lines: Wake the stones first. They have waited longer than I have.

aud.after.speaker: aud
lines: Snow landed on the roof this morning. I had forgotten that it makes a sound.
Please ring the bell. My arms are too old, and the one who brought the snow should ring it.

aud.bell.speaker: aud
lines: It hung silent for nine winters. Now it will not stop humming. Neither will I.

maren.raid.speaker: maren
lines: Not now, the hounds! Drive them off the fire, then we will talk.

maren.first.speaker: maren
lines: You came down the Run like the stories said, and you came down fighting. Good. I am Maren.
Out past the watching stone lies something old and huge. It holds the snow in the air. It is a Warden.
Varo went to watch it. Hounds have him pinned at his stone. And the boy, Tobin, has wandered off again. His tracks lead west to the spring.
A sled went east to the ridge for wood yesterday and has not come back. And Isolde needs you after dark.
Sleep by our fire when you need to. If you fall out there, you will wake beside it.

maren.again.speaker: maren
lines: Help Varo first. He is stubborn, but he is not foolish, and he has watched that thing longer than anyone.

maren.sled.speaker: maren
lines: Torn felt and no driver. Follow the prints to the ridge. If what made them is bigger than a hound, come back and tell me.

maren.tobin.speaker: maren
lines: You brought him back. He says you walk without a sound, and he had to listen hard for you.
Take this. It was a Shaper's before it was ours, and it never fit any of our hands.

maren.hounds.speaker: maren
lines: An old one, in the den? Then that is why they kept coming. She was feeding them.
The children walked to the spring this morning and no hound followed them. With her gone, the Warden will have fewer Shaped to call.

maren.night.speaker: maren
lines: My mother saw the Shapers once. Tall, and robed like you. They walked ahead of the weather.
Where they stopped, the snow came down. Where they went on, it followed.

maren.after.speaker: maren
lines: Listen. Snow is falling on the tents. I am too old to cry about weather, and here I am, crying.
Aud will want the bell rung. Go up to the monastery before the snow fills the Run.

tobin.found.speaker: tobin
lines: They went away. Were they yours? They didn't look like anybody's.
There's water under the ice. It's not moving either. But it talks, if you're quiet.
I'm not lost. I was listening.

options.text: Lead him back to the fire.
Let him listen a while longer.

tobin.walking.speaker: tobin
lines: Your feet don't make any sound. Mine do.

tobin.listening.speaker: tobin
lines: It's singing about the big ridge. Lots of voices, up on stone posts. One of them is cracked. You can hear it if you listen.
The cracked one will break first. I think it wants to.

tobin.again.speaker: tobin
lines: Do you have a face in there? Maren says no. I think it's just dark.

tobin.after.speaker: tobin
lines: The spring is talking now. It doesn't say words. It just talks.

isolde.day.speaker: isolde
lines: I am Isolde. This lantern was lit at the monastery nine winters ago. I carry it so the fire never has to start from nothing.
There are braziers at three of the shrines, and one at the edge of the Warden's ground. All cold since the snow stopped.
Come back after dark. I will put the flame in your lantern, if you can keep it alive to the braziers.

isolde.flame.speaker: isolde
lines: Hold the lantern still. There.
Walk, don't run. Don't get hit, and don't stand in the snow longer than you must. It is an old flame, and it tires.
And things will notice it. Cold things come to look at warm things.

isolde.relight.speaker: isolde
lines: It went out? It does that. It went out on me twice my first winter. Hold still.

isolde.night.speaker: isolde
lines: Sit, if you sit. I only know the slow songs. The fast ones need wind.

isolde.song.speaker: isolde
lines: Four flames, all leaning the same way. Sit.
This song is older than the camp. It is about a stone that listens past the far ridge, and another below the tarn. I never went.

isolde.after.speaker: isolde
lines: The flame leans now. I had never seen it lean.

varo.first.speaker: varo
lines: Good, someone came. I was running out of ways to stay still. Do you see it? For three days I thought it was a ridge.
When it wakes, pillars rise out of the snow around it, with crystals on them. The crystals heal it. You cannot hurt it while they stand.
When it stops moving and lifts its head, it is not resting. It throws its spines in every direction at once. Only stone stops them.
There is a small pillar here by my stone, a seedling. Practice on it. Climb it, break it, and when it stills, put my stone between you and it.

varo.again.speaker: varo
lines: The seedling. Climb it, break it, and get behind the stone when it brightens. Better to learn here than out there.

varo.seedling.speaker: varo
lines: You hid well. Anything that lives out here learns to hide the hard way.
The Warden has six pillars. Break them all, then freeze its seams and break those too. Take this. It will keep ice frozen in its joints a little longer.

varo.ready.speaker: varo
lines: Six crystals, then its seams. And stone between you and it whenever it stills.

varo.after.speaker: varo
lines: It is a hill now. A good hill. I will tell them it lay down on its own. They would not believe the rest.
Far below, a long white ridge breathes once, slowly, and is still.
Far off, the first snow in nine winters reaches the ground.
The note rolls out over the steppe, and the snow carries it far.

maren.early.speaker: maren
lines: A robe with no one in it. Stand by the fire, then. The hounds have been circling since dusk, and they will come again.

osk.raid.speaker: osk
lines: Not now. Hounds. Get them off the sled and then we will talk prices.

osk.first.speaker: osk
lines: I am Osk. That sled is mine, and so is what is on it. Salves, mostly. A tonic or two, for the cold.
Marks are the only coin out here. Old Shaper silver. Bring me rime cores, if you find any, and I will pay for them. But the smith in Hearn will pay you more, in work, if you keep them.

quests.title: The Empty Robe
quests.summary: Something has woken in the last Shaper's robe. It is you.

steps.journal: Talk to Aud at the monastery. She kept watch over the last Shaper.
Use a stone's own gesture on it: Crystallize, Sweep or Ribbon. There are three stones in the hall.
Go to the bottom of the steps. The stone woke something there.
Rest at the shrine by the east wall. If I fall, I will wake there.
Take the Shapers' Run down to the Pilgrims' Fire: nine gates on one long slope. Hold right mouse to surf.

optional.journal: Wake all three stones in the hall.
Look at the plain below the Run. Something lies across it.

quests.title: The Pilgrims' Fire
quests.summary: Hounds are attacking the last pilgrims' camp.

steps.journal: Go to the Pilgrims' Fire. Drive off the hounds before they reach the tents.
Talk to Old Maren. She leads the pilgrims and may know why the snow hangs.

quests.title: The Watching Stone
quests.summary: Varo went to watch the Warden and is trapped by hounds.

steps.journal: Go to the Watching Stone, east of the fire. Kill the hounds pinning Varo.
Talk to Varo. He has watched the Warden longer than anyone.
Break the seedling pillar by Varo's stone. Climb it (hold right mouse at its foot), break its crystal, then hide behind the stone when it stills and brightens.
Talk to Varo. He saw you break the seedling.

quests.title: The Held Snow
quests.summary: A Warden lies across the steppe and holds the snow in the air.

steps.journal: Release the Warden. Climb its six pillars and break their crystals. Then freeze its seams, break them, and wear it down. When it stills and lifts its head, get behind stone. If I fall, it lies down and waits.

quests.title: First Snow
quests.summary: The Warden has lain down. Motion is returning to the steppe.

steps.journal: Go to the Pilgrims' Fire. The snow is falling again.
Talk to Old Maren at the fire. She is waiting.
Ring the monastery bell. Aud asked that the one who brought the snow ring it.

quests.title: A Trail in the Snow
quests.summary: A pilgrim child has wandered away from the fire.

steps.journal: Follow the small footprints west across the frozen tarn to the Sleeping Spring.
Tobin is on the ice at the spring, and two hounds are circling him. Kill them.
The hounds are gone. Talk to Tobin. He is still listening to the ice.
Lead Tobin back to the fire, or leave him listening. He follows if you do not leave him behind.

optional.journal: When the steppe moves again, return to the Sleeping Spring.

quests.title: The Den Mother
quests.summary: A wood sled went east to the ridge and did not come back.

steps.journal: Find the sled. Maren says it went east toward the ridge for wood.
Many hound prints lead from the wreck to the ridge. Follow them to the den and kill what lives there.
The den is empty. Tell Old Maren what you found.

quests.title: Echoes of the Shapers
quests.summary: Echo stones stand hidden across the steppe. Each remembers a Shaper's gesture.

steps.journal: Find the three nearest echo stones. They answer only up close. Stand at one and give it the gesture it remembers.
Find the other three echo stones. They stand farther out and higher up.

optional.journal: Rest at all five shrines on the steppe.

quests.title: Carry the Flame
quests.summary: Isolde keeps the last flame from the monastery. The braziers have been cold for nine winters.

steps.journal: Go to Isolde after dark. She will light my lantern from hers.
Carry the flame to the four cold braziers: three at shrines, one at the edge of the Warden's ground. It gutters if I hurry and dies if I am hit. If it dies, Isolde will relight it.
All four braziers burn. Go to Isolde after dark. She will play.

quests.title: The Shapers' Run
quests.summary: The Shapers rode this slope faster than anyone since.

steps.journal: Ride all nine gates of the Run in under 31 seconds.
Ride the Run in under 26.5 seconds.
Ride the Run in under 23 seconds, the way the Shapers did.

echo-frost-hold.name: Echo of the Held Breath
echo-frost-hold.effect: Frozen joints and Shaped stay frozen 40% longer.
echo-frost-hold.text: What is held can be held a little longer.

echo-frost-surf.name: Echo of the Running Water
echo-frost-surf.effect: Snow-surf keeps its speed longer on flats.
echo-frost-surf.text: Water knows which way is down.

echo-frost-still.name: Echo of the Still Stone
echo-frost-still.effect: Focus returns faster while standing still.
echo-frost-still.text: The stones were patient. So are you.

echo-frost-sweep.name: Echo of the Open Hand
echo-frost-sweep.text: The hand remembers how far it reached.

lore-shapers-walked.title: They Walked Ahead of the Weather
lore-shapers-walked.text: The Shapers did not command the snow. They walked, and the snow followed, the way a dog follows someone it loves. As told by Old Maren.

lore-spring.title: The Sleeping Spring
lore-spring.text: Under the ice, the water still has the shape it had when the last Shaper died: mid-ripple, waiting to finish the motion.

lore-five-stones.title: The Five Stones
lore-five-stones.text: Each shrine marks where a Shaper stood still for a night. It was the only rest they allowed themselves. The stones kept it for them.

lore-slow-songs.title: The Slow Songs
lore-slow-songs.text: The pilgrims' songs lost their quick verses as the wind died. Isolde says the quick verses were about weather, and no one remembers what weather sounded like.

lore-shapers-run.title: The Shapers' Run
lore-shapers-run.text: The first Shapers did not walk down from the monastery. They leaned, and the snow carried them. The slope was cut afterward to match.

lore-spring-voice.title: What Tobin Heard
lore-spring-voice.text: Under the ice, the spring says one word, over and over. Tobin will not repeat it. He says it is not for people.

lore-stones-heard.title: Six Voices
lore-stones-heard.text: Six stones, left by six Shapers who stopped to speak where no one would pass. Together they say: we left the snow to you.

lore-hounds.title: The Den Mother
lore-hounds.text: The Shaped are what a stilled place dreams of itself: hungry because everything is still, quick because nothing else is. The old ones grow frost armor that turns blows aside. Only cold can reach them.

lore-echo-frost-1.title: Echo Stone 1
lore-echo-frost-1.text: The first Shaper stood here to see how far the steppe went. It went farther.

lore-echo-frost-2.title: Echo Stone 2
lore-echo-frost-2.text: Do not trust a calm slope. Trust the one that leans.

lore-echo-frost-3.title: Echo Stone 3
lore-echo-frost-3.text: I buried my name here. It was not shameful. It was heavy.

lore-echo-frost-4.title: Echo Stone 4
lore-echo-frost-4.text: The water under the tarn counted my steps. I stopped at one hundred and one.

lore-echo-frost-5.title: Echo Stone 5
lore-echo-frost-5.text: I turned where the wind turned. It made me kinder.

lore-echo-frost-6.title: Echo Stone 6
lore-echo-frost-6.text: The last of us wrote nothing. This stone is the note.

lore-bell.title: The Bell
lore-bell.text: The bell was cast to ring once each winter, when the first snow reached the monastery steps. It last rang the winter before the last Shaper died. Since then it has hung there, waiting, like the snow.

barks._comment: Ambient lines a Veiled says as the Wraith passes (systems/barks.js): the first entry whose `when` matches, one per NPC every ~2 minutes. DRAFT for the user's review.

lines: The wind is in the cloister again. I keep stopping to listen.
Nine winters of sweeping, and now the snow blows in faster than I can sweep.
The steps are clear. Go on. His body will keep.
The Shaper wore that robe for sixty years. He never once ran.
Careful. This floor echoes every step.
I am still here, keeping the hall.
Snow on my hood. I had forgotten how heavy it is.
The children are trying to catch it on their tongues. Let them.
Get behind the fire, all of you!
Protect the tents! Keep them away from the tents!
Sit, if a robe can sit. The fire is for anyone.
Count the tents for me. My eyes fail at night.
We came for the Shaper. We stayed for the quiet.
Old knees, old snow. Neither moves.
Is it far? It feels far.
I can walk. I just walk slowly.
I told them you'd find me. Nobody believed me.
Can I follow you again? Not far. Just to the echo stones.
Your hands look cold, even from here.
Maren says not to stare. I'm not staring. I'm looking.
Keep it out of the wind. And don't hurry.
It burns smaller in your hand than in mine. That's all right.
The lyre goes out of tune in the cold. I play it anyway.
Every lantern is a small promise, you know.
I trim the wick every hour. Old habit, from when the wind still blew it out.
Light carries a long way here. Farther than voices.
It's lying down. I watched it for three years and it never once lay down.
I could walk home now. I think I'll stand a little longer.
Watch the spines on its back. They glow before it breaks loose.
Stone stops it. Nothing else I've seen does.
Don't wave. It sees movement.
Down there. The white ridge that isn't a ridge.
